verdict.rationale: Poly documents team Shared Drives with their own members and roles, plus sharing files or folders with specific people. Parallel edits are preserved as conflict revisions that can be opened and restored, so nobody's work is lost. But there is no evidence of real-time co-editing or automatic merging, so users must reconcile conflicting versions themselves. missing for 10: real-time collaborative editing or automatic merge of concurrent edits, explicit documentation that collaborators get edit permissions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can share a vault or space with collaborators and edit notes together without stepping on each other's changes

citations.quote: A Shared Drive is its own storage space with its own members, roles, and archive.
Share a file or folder when the content belongs to you and you want specific people — or anyone with a link — to see it.
Any parallel edits are stored as conflict revisions
Even conflicting edits are preserved, so you can recover any version of any file at any time.
